issues.legal_issue: The National Green Tribunal may exercise jurisdiction only when a substantial question relating to the environment arises from implementation of an enactment listed in Schedule I to the National Green Tribunal Act.

Environmental concerns or reliance on the precautionary principle, without an alleged violation of a specific statutory environmental obligation under a Schedule I enactment, do not confer jurisdiction on the National Green Tribunal.

The National Green Tribunal exceeded its jurisdiction by directing revision of an approved township master plan and imposing environmental clearance and construction conditions where no qualifying substantial environmental question was established.
